desc: Derive the precise recurrence: for each distinct value x, answer = max subarray sum over segments of nums split at indices where nums[i]==x; also handle "no operation" (plain Kadane) and the non-empty constraint (skip x if it equals all elements).
Analyze complexity: per-x full scan is O(n·distinct) worst case — too slow; segment tree range-max-subarray queries give O((n + distinct) log n) = O(n log n) total.
Design segment tree: nodes store (sum, prefix, suffix, best); associative non-commutative combine; iterative query with left/right accumulators; identity (0, -inf, -inf, -inf); skip empty gaps.
Implement the solution in the given starter code: build segment tree, group indices by value with a dict, iterate gaps per value, track global max including the no-deletion case.

Test against examples (nums=[-3,2,-2,-1,3,-2,3] → 7; [1,2,3,4] → 10) plus edge cases: all negatives, single element, all same value, alternating two values, and a large random array validated against a brute-force O(n · distinct) checker.
